Summary

The escalation began in spring 2022 following a series of attacks by Palestinians inside Israel that killed 19 Israelis between March 22 and May 7. Israel responded by launching 'Operation Break the Wave'—near-nightly military raids into West Bank cities and refugee camps, particularly Jenin and Nablus. These cities had become centers of renewed armed Palestinian resistance with the emergence of groups like the Jenin Brigades (founded September 2021), the Lions' Den in Nablus, and the Balata Brigades. The Israeli operations involved massive deployments of troops, bulldozers destroying infrastructure and roads, use of live ammunition in densely populated areas, and increasingly, aerial bombardment including drone strikes. By the end of 2022, 220 Palestinians had been killed including 48 children—the highest annual toll since the Second Intifada ended in 2005.

The violence was not limited to armed confrontations. According to Middle East Eye's analysis, the majority of Palestinian casualties in 2022 were likely unarmed at the time of their death. At least 95 Palestinians were shot by Israeli soldiers as bystanders during army raids or while participating in anti-occupation demonstrations. Seven women and girls were killed, including 15-year-old Jana Zakarneh shot twice in the face while playing with her cat on her rooftop, and 15-year-old Fulla al-Masalma killed a day before her birthday. The most internationally significant killing was that of Shireen Abu Akleh, Al Jazeera's veteran Palestinian correspondent, shot in the head on May 11, 2022 while covering a raid in Jenin. Despite wearing a clearly marked PRESS vest and standing with other journalists, Abu Akleh was killed by Israeli fire. The UN Commission of Inquiry investigated and concluded 'on reasonable grounds that Israeli forces used lethal force without justification under international human rights law and, intentionally or recklessly, violated Abu Akleh's right to life.'

The violence intensified further in 2023. In January, a raid on Jenin killed 10 Palestinians including a 61-year-old woman shot through the neck while watching from her bedroom window. In February, 11 Palestinians were killed in Nablus including civilians shot in the back while fleeing. In July, Israel conducted its largest West Bank operation in 20 years—a 14-hour assault on Jenin refugee camp using drones, helicopter gunships, and hundreds of troops, killing 12 and forcing 500 families to flee. By December 2023, Doctors Without Borders declared it 'the deadliest year for Palestinians in the West Bank in recorded history' with 507 killed including 127 children. The UN Commission found Israeli forces systematically violated international law by applying combat rules to law enforcement situations, using disproportionate force, failing to distinguish between civilians and combatants, obstructing medical care, and conducting what amounted to extrajudicial executions. Meanwhile, settler violence also surged—the UN recorded over 800 settler attacks on Palestinians between October 2022 and May 2024, often occurring with Israeli military acquiescence or participation.

The Commission has documented alarming trends in Israeli security forces' use of force...The operations in Jenin in 2023 appear to have included the use of unnecessary and disproportionate force.' — UN Commission Press Release, October 16, 2023
Shatha ZakarnehDescribing daughter's killing: 'Jana was on our roof playing with her cat. She wasn't protesting, she wasn't near any fighting. An Israeli sniper shot her twice in the face. My daughter was just a child playing with her pet. How can they say she was a threat? They killed her for no reason except that she was Palestinian.' Jana died January 2023. — Family testimony to media and human rights organizations
Al Jazeera (institutional)Statement after Shireen Abu Akleh's killing: 'We hold the Israeli government and the Israeli occupation forces responsible for the killing of Shireen. Emphasized she was clearly marked as press. — Al Jazeera Official Statement, May 11, 2022

Majida died in January 2023 Jenin raid. — Family testimony documented in reports

War crimes

Unlawful Killing of Journalist Shireen Abu AklehMay 11, 2022: Al Jazeera correspondent shot in head while covering Jenin raid. Wearing clearly marked PRESS vest, standing with journalists. UN Commission concluded 'on reasonable grounds that Israeli forces used lethal force without justification under international human rights law and, intentionally or recklessly, violated Abu Akleh's right to life.' Identified Duvdevan Unit as likely responsible. Intentional or reckless killing of clearly marked journalist is war crime. — 📄 UN Commission Findings ↑
Extrajudicial ExecutionsPalestinians accuse Israeli forces of assassination policy targeting armed group leaders. In three incidents in 2022, Israeli forces fatally shot 9 Palestinian fighters while inside vehicles in what Palestinians called 'field executions.' Pattern of targeted killings without arrest attempts. Video from Feb 2023 Nablus shows two men shot in back while fleeing—indicative of willful killing. — 📄 MEE Investigation ↑
Unnecessary and Disproportionate ForceUN Commission concluded several 2023 Jenin operations 'appear to have included use of unnecessary and disproportionate force by Israeli security forces.' Includes use of drones, helicopters, hundreds of troops in densely populated refugee camps. Artillery-like force in law enforcement context violates international human rights law. — 📄 UN Commission Report ↑
Killing of 78+ ChildrenAt least 78 children killed 2022-2023 including many unarmed bystanders. Jana Zakarneh (15) shot twice in face while playing with cat on rooftop. Mahmoud Samoudi (12) shot during raid. Zaid Ghonaim (15) shot while hiding in parking garage. Wasim Abu Jaes (16) crushed by military vehicle. Willful killing of children violates Fourth Geneva Convention Article 147. — 📄 Multiple Documented Cases ↑
Obstruction of Medical CareSystematic pattern of Israeli forces firing on ambulances, preventing medical personnel from reaching wounded, delaying evacuations. Jan 2023 Jenin: ambulances fired upon, tear gas shot at hospital pediatric ward. May 2023: medical sources report forces restricted ambulance movement. Denying medical care to wounded violates Geneva Conventions. — 📄 Multiple Incident Reports ↑
Hospital Raid with Perfidy (War Crime)January 2024: Israeli commandos disguised as medical staff and Muslim women entered Jenin hospital, shot dead three Palestinians inside. UN experts: may amount to war crimes. Perfidy (feigning protected status to kill) explicitly prohibited under Geneva Conventions Additional Protocol I Article 37. Killing wounded even if militants also violates IHL. — 📄 Documentation ↑
Misapplication of Legal FrameworkUN Commission finding: Israel applies combat rules (IHL conduct of hostilities) to law enforcement situations in West Bank, contrary to international law. This results in use of lethal force not justified under human rights law governing law enforcement. Systematic policy decision enabling unlawful killings. — 📄 UN Commission Legal Analysis ↑
Destruction of Civilian PropertySystematic use of bulldozers to destroy roads, infrastructure, homes during raids. July 2023 Jenin: massive destruction of refugee camp infrastructure. Pattern of destruction far exceeding military necessity. Extensive destruction not justified by military operations is grave breach under Fourth Geneva Convention Article 147. — 📄 Documentation ↑

Legal classification

Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core ViolationLaw Enforcement vs. Conduct of Hostilities: UN Commission determined Israel unlawfully applies IHL rules on conduct of hostilities to law enforcement in West Bank. Correct framework is international human rights law which strictly limits use of lethal force.
International Humanitarian Law ViolationsFourth Geneva Convention Article 27: Protected persons 'shall be treated humanely...protected against all acts of violence.' Killing of 78+ children, journalists, medical obstruction violate this core protection.
UN Commission Findings (October 2023)Shireen Abu Akleh: Commission found 'on reasonable grounds that Israeli forces used lethal force without justification...and, intentionally or recklessly, violated Abu Akleh's right to life.'
Specific Protected Persons ViolationsChildren: Convention on Rights of Child and Fourth Geneva Convention Article 24 provide special protection. Killing 78+ children, many unarmed, violates these protections.
Accountability RequirementsDuty to Investigate: Geneva Conventions require States investigate grave breaches. Israel has systematically failed to conduct meaningful investigations.
Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core ViolationRight to Life (ICCPR Article 6): Lethal force only permissible when 'strictly necessary' to protect against imminent threat to life. UN found Israeli forces killed civilians not posing such threats—violations of right to life.
International Humanitarian Law ViolationsArticle 147 (Grave Breaches): 'Wilful killing...wilfully causing great suffering...extensive destruction...not justified by military necessity' are grave breaches. 500+ killings, property destruction meet threshold.
UN Commission Findings (October 2023)Jenin Operations: Several 2023 operations 'appear to have included unnecessary and disproportionate force.' Use of drones, helicopters in densely populated areas violates proportionality.
Specific Protected Persons ViolationsMedical Personnel: Geneva Conventions require protection of medical workers. Firing on ambulances, obstructing care, tear-gassing hospital violate absolute protections.
Accountability RequirementsCommand Responsibility: Senior military and political officials who knew or should have known of violations and failed to prevent/punish may bear criminal responsibility.
Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core ViolationBasic Principles on Use of Force and Firearms (1990): 'Intentional lethal use of firearms may only be made when strictly unavoidable in order to protect life.' Majority of West Bank killings do not meet this standard.
International Humanitarian Law ViolationsProtection of Journalists: Additional Protocol I Article 79 protects journalists as civilians. Killing of Shireen Abu Akleh—clearly marked press—is grave breach.
UN Commission Findings (October 2023)Pattern of Violations: 'Israel applies framework governing conduct of hostilities to law enforcement operations in West Bank, contrary to international law, resulting in civilians being killed and injured.'
Specific Protected Persons ViolationsWounded: Even wounded combatants protected once hors de combat. January 2024 hospital killings of wounded violate Common Article 3.
Accountability RequirementsICC Jurisdiction: International Criminal Court has jurisdiction over situation in Palestine. West Bank killings fall within investigation.
Misapplication of Legal Framework - Core ViolationSystematic Policy: Misapplication of legal framework is policy decision by Israeli government, not error. Enables systematic unlawful killings across entire territory.
International Humanitarian Law ViolationsPerfidy Prohibition: Additional Protocol I Article 37 prohibits feigning protected status to kill. January 2024 hospital raid with commandos disguised as medical staff constitutes perfidy—war crime.
UN Commission Findings (October 2023)Settler Violence: Commission documented increase in settler attacks on Palestinians, often with Israeli military acquiescence or participation—State responsibility for violations.
Specific Protected Persons ViolationsWomen and Families: Majida Obaid (61) shot in neck watching from window; Fulla al-Masalma (15) killed day before birthday—demonstrate indiscriminate nature of force.
Accountability RequirementsState Responsibility: Israel bears State responsibility for violations by its forces and for settler violence it fails to prevent.
